input.quote: 3.4 HDI's General Manager (as hereinafter defined), may upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company, have the right to inspect the records of the Company's General Manager reasonably related to the calculation of such payments during the Company's normal business hours. The fees incurred by HDI in connection with the inspection shall be borne by HDI.
input.rationale: Section 3.4 is the only provision binding us to an inspection, and it runs in HDI's favour as Vendor. It already satisfies two fallback elements on their material terms: 30 days' prior written notice (exceeding the 15-day floor) and HDI bearing the inspection cost without any underpayment trigger (more favourable than the 10 percent exception). However, it contains no frequency limit, so HDI could inspect our records repeatedly, which is walk-away territory (unlimited audits) and fails the fallback. The single surgical edit caps the right at once per year, bringing the clause to the fallback position; the remaining preferred refinements (independent confidentiality-bound auditor, off-site where possible, no system access) are not pursued because the clause is limited to records inspection and grants no access to our systems.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 3.4 gives HDI an unlimited right to inspect our records, so we have capped it at one inspection per year; the existing 30 days' written notice, business-hours limit and HDI-borne cost are acceptable and remain unchanged.
proposal.summary: Cap HDI's records inspection right at once per year
